evidence.source: CASE 報科學 (National Taiwan University Center for Science Education)
evidence.text: The author identifies rare, damaged Shang oracle-bone forms as 能, reading them as a bear-like pictograph whose head is reduced to an eye-shaped form, limbs linearized, and short tail retained. The author says the damaged occurrences do not establish use. In the transition to Western Zhou bronze, the head shifts toward 㠯, the body is rendered as 月 (肉), and the feet are placed side by side; later bronze, Chu and Qin slip, seal, and clerical forms remain comparatively recognizable. This is one side of a dispute over the Shang identification.
evidence.title: 獼猴與黑熊：甲骨文的「夒」、「猱」與「能」

evidence.source: 劉雲, Fudan University Center for Unearthed Documents and Ancient Chinese Characters
evidence.text: The author reports that scholars identify a Shang oracle-bone animal graph as 能, but argues the reading is doubtful and identifies it instead as 鷧 (cormorant). Cited differences include the neck/shoulder strokes, feet, tail, and head. The author says securely identifiable 能 first appears in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions and presents 能匋尊, 鬲比簋, 毛公厝鼎, and 番生簋 examples. This is a competing paleographic analysis, not a settled consensus.
evidence.title: 劉雲：釋“鷧”及相關諸字

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》, text hosted by Wikisource
evidence.field: 卷十, 能部; entry for 能
evidence.text: The Han dictionary defines 能 as a kind of bear with feet like a deer, segments it as 从肉㠯聲, and associates the animal's firmness and strength with 賢能 and 能傑. This documents the Han lexicographic analysis; it does not independently prove that the 㠯-like shape originated as a phonetic component, since paleographic analysis may interpret the shape as a transformed bear head.
evidence.title: 說文解字/10

evidence.text: The entry reports an early Western Zhou bronze use of 能 as a verb meaning ‘be able to’; it also cites 詩經·大雅·民勞 and later Warring States-era 左傳 examples for ability-related senses, plus a bear reading in a variant of 左傳·昭公七年. These attestations support early ability usage and a transmitted bear gloss, but do not establish a linear semantic path from bear to ability or secure the damaged Shang graph's use.
evidence.kind: dictionary report of cited historical attestations
evidence.title: 能(ノウ)とは？ 意味や使い方

evidence.text: The official character record for U+80FD lists kMandarin néng. This is current pronunciation metadata, not evidence of an ancient sound relationship.

gaps: The Shang oracle-bone reading remains disputed: one account identifies rare, damaged forms as 能 and another argues the graph is 鷧. The use of the damaged Shang forms cannot be established from the inspected account.

The earliest securely identified 能 graph is placed in Western Zhou bronze by the Fudan author, but no dated inscription proving the first occurrence or a precise date for the named example was recovered.

The bear noun and ability verb are separately attested in historical sources, but those sources do not establish a linear semantic extension or borrowing path between them. Shuowen's strength-based explanation is a Han-era account.

No independently established phonetic component in the early graph was found. Shuowen's 㠯聲 segmentation is preserved as the historical dictionary's analysis; in the graphic-history analysis, that shape may reflect the bear head's transformation. No component sound array is warranted.
The direct Unicode Unihan record verifies current néng. The provided local Baxter–Sagart rows preserve three distinct readings; no independent sound component is asserted.

No glyph image is proposed. Exact Commons file pages yielded cache misses when opened, and Xiaoxuetang's exact rendered image URL and record label could not be verified in the browser. The CC0 notice applies to query-interface glyph images and attributes, but no specific glyph image was selected.

limitations.text: Although searches surfaced exact Commons bronze-style 能 file descriptions and a Xiaoxuetang seal-form record, the browser could not open the exact asset pages or verify a direct original-image URL and specific source label. No candidate is selected without that provenance check.
